newsitem.title: FINLAND: Europe must stand by EMU terms, timetable - Dutch PM.
newsitem.headline: Europe must stand by EMU terms, timetable - Dutch PM.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Wednesday Europe must stand by the Maastricht treaty on economic and monetary union (EMU), by the entry criteria, the timetable and by the later agreed budget stability pact.
"We in Europe have to stick to what we agreed upon. We have the Maastricht treaty, we have a set of criteria, we have a timetable and we have a stability pact," Kok told a news conference here.
Kok was in Finland for a one-day visit as part of a tour of European capitals ahead of the European Union's June 16-17 summit in Amsterdam wrapping up the Dutch EU presidency.

"So these are the basic elements to be taken into account ... next year when we take decisions in the Ecofin council and the European council on who is going to take part in the third phase of EMU and who not," Kok said.
Neither the Maastricht treaty not subsequently agreed additions to it, like the budget stability pact, should be renegotiated, he said.
"There should be no renegotiation process of the treaty itself or of policy decisions that have been taken as a follow-up to the treaty."
Referring to the EU's inter-governmental conference (IGC), Kok said he did not expect "political problems for the IGC" as a result of the change of government in France.
"We intend to finalise the IGC process in Amsterdam," he said.
Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen told the news conference that the convergence criteria for membership of Europe's planned single currency should not be relaxed.
"We should absolutely not make the EMU process political in such a way that we would relax the criteria (or) relax pressure on the countries that have not yet made the criteria," he said.
"We assume that each and every member country wants to pass the criteria," Lipponen said.
Finland and the Netherlands are among the few EU member countries fulfilling the EMU criteria.

Asked about Sweden's decision on Tuesday to opt out of the first wave of countries joining EMU, Kok said he expected to address the issue at his meeting with Swedish government leaders in Stockholm on Thursday.
